description.summary: the compositor's channel to its desktop shell

protocol.description:
What passes between perspicax and perspicax-shell that no standard protocol carries: the person asked for a menu or a pie, or pressed a volume key, the config changed, the session should end, the keyboard's layouts and which is in use, and what the person chose in a window's menu.
Everything else the shell does, it does as any other client would. Its wallpaper, panel and menus are layer-shell surfaces, its taskbar speaks wlr-foreign-toplevel-management and its pager ext-workspace. That keeps this protocol small, and every piece of the shell replaceable by a program that speaks only the standard ones. A window's menu names the window and the workspace by the handles those two gave it, so this protocol has no names of its own for either.
The global is privileged: the compositor offers it only to the programs its [protocols] shell rule admits, and withdraws it, with finished, from a client a reload no longer admits. While the session is locked the compositor sends nothing and ignores every request.

interface.name: perspicax_shell_v1

description.summary: a shell's binding to the compositor

interface.description: Bound once by a shell. Several shells may bind it; each is told the same things.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop listening

request.description: The shell is done with this object. Nothing more is sent on it.

request.name: exit_session

description.summary: end the session

request.description: The person chose to log out. The compositor ends the session, as Ctrl+Alt+Backspace does, taking every client with it.

event.name: start_menu

description.summary: the person asked for the start menu

event.description:
A binding asked for the start menu: a tap of the Logo key, say. A shell shows its start menu on this monitor, or hides it if it is already showing, as a second tap does on Plasma.
The output is the monitor under the pointer, or null if this client has not bound that monitor's wl_output.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the monitor to show it on

event.name: root_menu

description.summary: the person asked for the root menu

event.description:
A binding asked for the root menu, the desktop's own menu that a right-click on the wallpaper also opens. A shell shows it at x, y, in logical pixels from the monitor's top-left corner, or hides it if it is already showing.
The position is where the pointer is, which a shell cannot see for itself while the pointer is over another client's window.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the monitor the pointer is on

event.name: reconfigure

description.summary: the config file changed

event.description: The person saved a config file whose shell settings differ from the ones this shell started with. A shell reads the file again and applies it in place.

event.name: finished

description.summary: the compositor withdrew this object

event.description: This client is no longer admitted: a reload changed the rule. The compositor sends nothing more and ignores every request; the shell should destroy the object.

request.name: set_layout

description.summary: switch the keyboard's layout

request.description: The person chose a layout on the shell: clicked its indicator, say. The compositor switches the keyboard to layout index, counted from 0 in the order the layout events named them. An index past the last is ignored.

event.name: layout

description.summary: one of the keyboard's layouts

event.description: Sent for each of the keyboard's layouts in order, from index 0, when the object is bound and again whenever the keymap changes, then layouts_done.

arg.name: name
arg.summary: xkb's name for it, as English (US)

arg.name: short
arg.summary: a label for a panel, as US

event.name: layouts_done

description.summary: every layout has been named

event.description: The layout events since the last layouts_done are the keyboard's layouts now, and replace any named before.

event.name: active_layout

description.summary: the layout in use

event.description: Sent after layouts_done, and whenever the layout in use changes.

arg.name: index
arg.summary: the layout in use, counted from 0

event.name: pie_menu

description.summary: the person asked for a pie menu

event.description:
A binding asked for the pie menu of this name, one of the config's [shell.pie.menus]. A shell shows it centred at x, y, in logical pixels from the monitor's top-left corner, or hides it if that pie is the one showing; another pie showing gives way to it.
The position is where the pointer is, which a shell cannot see for itself while the pointer is over another client's window.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the monitor the pointer is on

description.summary: what a volume key asks of the sound

entry.name: up
entry.summary: the output's volume up a step

entry.name: down
entry.summary: the output's volume down a step

entry.name: mute
entry.summary: the output muted, or its sound back

event.name: volume

description.summary: the person pressed a volume key

event.description: A binding asked for the sound to change: XF86AudioRaiseVolume, say. A shell changes the default output's volume by its step, or mutes it or brings its sound back, or the default input's, as its mixer would, and may show what it did. The compositor holds no volume of its own; the sound server is the shell's to ask.

enum.name: window_state

description.summary: what a window is made

enum.description: What the person made of a window, by a key, a titlebar button or its menu, beyond what the taskbar's own protocol tells. A bit a later version adds is sent only to a shell bound at that version.

entry.name: on_top
entry.summary: kept in front of the other windows

enum.name: window_capabilities

description.summary: what can be made of a window

enum.description: Which of the requests below can act on a window, so that a menu need not offer what would do nothing.

entry.name: workspace
entry.summary: it has a workspace of its own: set_sticky and send_to_workspace act

entry.name: shade
entry.summary: its frame is the compositor's and it is not fullscreen: set_shaded acts

event.name: toplevel_state

description.summary: what a window is made, and where it is

event.description:
Sent for each window this client holds a handle on, from zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1, once that handle has had its first done; and again whenever any of it changes, at most once a turn of the compositor's loop, so that a menu opened shows the window as it is. A tab behind another is told its group's, as the tab in front holds it. Nothing is sent while the session is locked, and what changed meanwhile is told once it is unlocked.
The workspace is this client's handle on it, from ext_workspace_manager_v1: null for a sticky window, for one with no workspace of its own, and while this client holds no handle on it.

arg.name: capabilities
arg.summary: what can be made of it

request.name: set_sticky

description.summary: put a window on every workspace, or on one

request.description:
The person chose Sticky in a window's menu. The compositor puts the window on every workspace, or, with sticky 0, back on the one its monitor shows, as the toggle-sticky binding does.
The window is named by the handle this client holds on it, from zwlr_foreign_toplevel_manager_v1. A tab behind another is in its group's place: what is asked of it is done to the tab in front. A window that is so already, one with no workspace of its own, a handle the compositor has closed, and a client no longer admitted to foreign-toplevel-management are each ignored, as every request is while the session is locked.

request.name: set_on_top

description.summary: keep a window in front of the others, or not

request.description: The person chose Always on top in a window's menu. The compositor keeps the window in front of the other windows, or, with on_top 0, lets it go back among them, as the toggle-on-top binding does, and raises it either way. Ignored as set_sticky is.

arg.name: on_top
arg.summary: 1 to keep it in front, 0 to let it go

request.name: set_shaded

description.summary: roll a window up to its titlebar, or down

request.description: The person chose Shade in a window's menu. The compositor rolls the window up to its titlebar, or, with shaded 0, back down, drawn rolling as the toggle-shade binding draws it. Only a window whose frame the compositor draws, and that is not fullscreen, rolls up. Ignored as set_sticky is.

arg.name: shaded
arg.summary: 1 to roll it up, 0 to roll it down

request.name: send_to_workspace

description.summary: move a window to a workspace, and stay

request.description:
The person chose a workspace in a window's menu. The compositor moves the window there and leaves the view where it is, as the send-to-workspace binding does; a sticky window is on that one alone from then on.
The workspace is named by the handle this client holds on it, from ext_workspace_manager_v1. When each monitor has workspaces of its own, a workspace of another monitor's is ignored: the window stays on its monitor. Otherwise ignored as set_sticky is, and so is the workspace the window is on already.
